messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT P1 — hosted-runtime KVCache OOM (high error rate). Auto-detected by memory-sentinel. Region: us-west-2. Starting pager. Root event: kv_cache.used_memory spike -> OOMs on several shards.

alice (oncall): I'm on it. grabbing logs and connecting to the runtime dashboard.

devan (runtime): seeing a correlated jump in `prefetch.requests` and `batch.window_ms`. Looks like a long-prompt campaign causing runaway KV growth. Example request lengths in the sample: 250k tokens on a small session.

maria (sre): Confirmed — memory per shard jumped from ~28GB -> 80GB in under 2m on three pods. We have immediate OOM kills on pod ids: pod-rt-3a, pod-rt-7b, pod-rt-9c.

alice (oncall): @devan @maria what's the blast radius? Any customer-facing 5xxs?

neil (support): I'm seeing a 12% spike in 5xxs for hosted text-gen in us-west-2 and a handful of large customers reporting timeouts. Ticket spike from orgs: org-zen, org-qualia.

devan (runtime): short answer: yes. Some requests hit `500` due to OOM while KV growth was unbounded. Error rate peaked ~18% for a 4 minute window.

ops-tilt-bot: Link to runtime dashboard: https://tilt.redwood.internal/d/rt/kvcache-memory?from=2200001000&to=2200001400

maria (sre): mitigation plan: 1) throttle prefetch on hosted runtime globally 2) enforce a hard `max_context_tokens` per session 3) temporary routing to smaller-model fallback for impacted routes. Need one engineer to patch the runtime config and another to update routing.

jamie (eng): I'll take routing fallback. Flipping route to `model-reduced` for routes `text-gen/*` in us-west-2.

devan (runtime): I'll push a hotpatch to disable aggressive prefetch and lower batch window. Proposed runtime flags: 
```
kvcache.prefetch.enabled=false
kvcache.prefetch.max_outstanding=8
batch.window_ms=8
session.max_context_tokens=65536
```
I'll apply via k8s patch to the hosted-runtime configmap and restart pods gracefully.

alice (oncall): Please share exact kubectl commands here for audit.

devan (runtime): running: 
```
kubectl -n hosted-runtime patch configmap runtime-config -p '{"data":{"kvcache.prefetch.enabled":"false","kvcache.prefetch.max_outstanding":"8","batch.window_ms":"8","session.max_context_tokens":"65536"}}'
kubectl -n hosted-runtime rollout restart deployment/hosted-runtime --selector=shard=us-west-2
```
Applying now.

ops-tilt-bot: `kubectl patch` acknowledged. Rolling restart started (pods terminating gracefully).

maria (sre): I'm temporarily increasing eviction aggressiveness to protect control-plane: `kvcache.eviction_aggressiveness=high` so we don't thrash allocs.

jamie (eng): Route flip applied for `text-gen/*` to `model-reduced` in us-west-2. Canary 10% -> 100% within 60s.

neil (support): Notifying affected customers: sending template update to org-zen and org-qualia. 

alice (oncall): Memory trend is coming down on the dashboard. Error rate dropped back to baseline ~2% after hotpatch and routing fallback. Confirming no further OOMs in last 4 minutes.

devan (runtime): Logs from pod-rt-3a around spike show repeated huge context prepend calls: 
```
2026-03-15T14:02:15Z [rt] session=abcd1234 prefetch=256k tokens queued
2026-03-15T14:02:16Z [rt] kvcache.insert size=48MB entries=12000
2026-03-15T14:02:17Z [rt] OOM: alloc failure while inserting kvpage
```
Looks like a single session with an attacker/client that sent a huge concatenated prompt via the API. We need throttles at ingress too.

maria (sre): Good catch. I'll put a temporary API-layer check to drop sessions with >100k token single requests and return `429` with guidance. That will mitigate abusive clients until we have better pacing controls.

alice (oncall): Who wants ownership for postmortem? We need RCA, customer impact table, and permanent mitigations (ingress throttles, prefetch backpressure, session hard caps).

devan (runtime): I'll do the runtime side of the RCA and a proposed design doc for backpressure and prefetch budget.

jamie (eng): I'll do routing/fallback playbook updates and test the smaller-model fallback to ensure quality thresholds.

maria (sre): I'll run the customer impact calc and coordinate follow-up comms. Initial numbers: ~12% of requests in us-west-2 experienced elevated error rate for ~4m, ~423k total requests in window, ~50k affected. Two paying customers reported timeouts; we opened support tickets.

neil (support): Updated customers: org-zen asked for timeline/compensation; they've paused heavy workloads. We're flagging for account team.

ops-tilt-bot: Post-hotfix metrics: memory usage graph: https://tilt.redwood.internal/graph/kvcache/mem/2200001200-2200001400 (showing rapid decline).

alice (oncall): We're stable. Gradually reverting emergency flags? I propose: keep prefetch disabled and `session.max_context_tokens=65536` for 24h, revert routing after 1h if metrics stable.

devan (runtime): Agreed. I'll keep eviction high for 30m then lower to normal. We'll also add an alert tweak: trigger if single-session kvcache growth > 50MB/s for >30s.

maria (sre): Scheduled follow-up meeting in 2 hours to collect artifacts and start the RCA: https://calendar.redwood/internal/meet/rca-2200001111

jamie (eng): Quick note for postmortem: add regression test that simulates long prompt batching to ensure prefetch doesn't blow past configured budgets.

alice (oncall): Great work team. Closing pager for now. If anyone sees a regression re-ping here. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident P1 resolved — mitigation applied. Please submit postmortem links and tags once available.

maria (sre): Postmortem owners: runtime=devan, routing=jamie, customer-impact=maria. Will create doc in #incidents-postmortems and link here.

neil (support): I'll draft customer emails and provide a list of affected orgs.

alice (oncall): Closing thread — moving to post-incident channel for follow-up.
